title: La comida
goal: Talk about food in detail, follow and give a simple recipe, and use the impersonal se.

lessons.title: At the market
lessons.notes:
More food words for shopping and cooking. Some differ across the Spanish-speaking world:
**los frijoles** (beans) are **las judías** or **las alubias** in Spain and **los porotos** in Chile and Argentina.
**la papa** (potato) is **la patata** in Spain.
Uncountable foods go without an article after **comer, comprar, necesitar**: **Compro pollo y arroz.** With **gustar** they take one: **Me gusta el arroz.**
Amounts: **un kilo de**, **medio kilo de** (half a kilo).

sentences.es: Quisiera un kilo de tomates, por favor.
sentences.en: I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, please.

sentences.es: No como carne, pero como pescado.
sentences.en: I don't eat meat, but I eat fish.
Today we're having chicken with rice for dinner.
accept_en: Tonight we're having chicken and rice.
Today we have chicken with rice for dinner.

sentences.en: In Mexico we eat a lot of beans.
accept_en: In Mexico we eat lots of beans.

sentences.en: You have to eat more vegetables.
accept_en: We need to eat more vegetables.

sentences.en: I need potatoes, onions and garlic.
How much is a kilo of potatoes?
accept_en: How much does a kilo of potatoes cost?

sentences.es: Para el desayuno como dos huevos.
sentences.en: For breakfast I eat two eggs.
accept_en: I have two eggs for breakfast.

lessons.title: In the kitchen
lessons.notes:
Cooking verbs are mostly regular -ar verbs:
**cortar** (to cut) · **mezclar** (to mix) · **agregar** (to add; Spain: **añadir**) · **lavar** (to wash)
Two with stem changes: **calentar** (to heat, e -> ie: **caliento**) and **freír** (to fry, e -> i: **frío** - same spelling as "cold"!). **hervir** (to boil) is e -> ie: **hierve**.
Things you cook with: **la olla** (pot), **la sartén** (frying pan - feminine), **el horno** (oven).
Remember **lavar** without **se** is washing something else: **Lavo las verduras.**

sentences.es: Corto la cebolla y el tomate.
sentences.en: I cut the onion and the tomato.
accept_en: I chop the onion and the tomato.
I'm cutting the onion and the tomato.

sentences.es: Mezclo los huevos con la leche.
sentences.en: I mix the eggs with the milk.
I add a little water.
accept_en: I add a bit of water.

sentences.es: Mi mamá calienta la sopa en la olla.
sentences.en: My mum heats the soup in the pot.
accept_en: My mom heats up the soup in the pot.
My mother heats the soup in the saucepan.

sentences.es: Frío las papas en la sartén.
sentences.en: I fry the potatoes in the frying pan.
accept_en: I fry the potatoes in the pan.

sentences.es: El agua hierve en la olla.
sentences.en: The water is boiling in the pot.
accept_en: The water boils in the pot.
The water's boiling in the pot.

sentences.en: He washes the vegetables well.

sentences.es: El pollo está en el horno.
sentences.en: The chicken is in the oven.
Did you heat the oven?
accept_en: Did you heat up the oven?

lessons.title: How it's done: se
lessons.notes:
Recipes and signs often don't say who does the action. Spanish uses **se** + the verb in the **él** or **ellos** form - the **impersonal se**:
**Se corta la cebolla.** = The onion is cut / You cut the onion.
**Se cortan las papas.** = The potatoes are cut (plural thing -> plural verb).
**Aquí se habla español.** = Spanish is spoken here.
**¿Cómo se dice...?** = How do you say...?
It's like English "you" or "one" in general statements. Look at what follows: one thing -> **se corta**; several -> **se cortan**.

items.note: e -> i: sirvo. Se sirve = it's served.
The spice. The vegetable is el pimiento / el chile.

sentences.en: First you cut the onion.
Then you add the tomatoes.

sentences.es: Se calienta el aceite en la sartén.
sentences.en: You heat the oil in the frying pan.
accept_en: The oil is heated in the frying pan.
Heat the oil in the pan.

sentences.en: You add salt and pepper.
It's served with rice.
Spanish is spoken here.
How do you say "oven" in Spanish?

sentences.es: Se mezclan dos cucharadas de azúcar con la leche.
sentences.en: You mix two spoonfuls of sugar with the milk.
accept_en: Two spoonfuls of sugar are mixed with the milk.
Mix two tablespoons of sugar with the milk.

sentences.en: You don't need much salt.

lessons.title: How does it taste?
lessons.notes:
Hunger and thirst use **tener**: **tengo hambre** (I'm hungry), **tengo sed** (I'm thirsty).
To say how food tastes, use **estar** for this dish right now and **ser** for food in general:
**La sopa está rica.** = The soup is (tastes) delicious.
**El chocolate es dulce.** = Chocolate is sweet.
**probar** (o -> ue) without **se** means to taste or try food: **¿Quieres probar?** Compare **probarse** = to try on clothes.
And remember **la receta**: a recipe in the kitchen, a prescription at the doctor's.

items.note: o -> ue: pruebo. With food; probarse is for clothes.
demasiado dulce = too sweet; demasiada sal = too much salt.

sentences.en: I'm very hungry. Shall we eat?
accept_en: I'm really hungry. Shall we eat?

sentences.es: ¿Tienes sed? Hay agua en la mesa.
sentences.en: Are you thirsty? There's water on the table.
Do you want to taste the soup?
accept_en: Do you want to try the soup?
Would you like to try the soup?

sentences.en: The food is delicious.
This dish is very spicy.

sentences.es: El chocolate es demasiado dulce para mí.
sentences.en: Chocolate is too sweet for me.
accept_en: The chocolate is too sweet for me.

sentences.en: The soup is very salty.

sentences.es: Mi abuela tiene una receta de pollo muy buena.
sentences.en: My grandmother has a very good chicken recipe.
accept_en: My grandma has a really good chicken recipe.

sentences.es: Probé un plato típico de Perú.
sentences.en: I tried a typical dish from Peru.
accept_en: I tasted a typical Peruvian dish.
I tried a typical Peruvian dish.
